causal.assumptions_right: Defining the invalidation as a full bounce retrace or SOFR March 2027 through 4.435 gave a clear exit. Equity risk appetite was not the thing that broke: the S&P is still 7520.93 and VIX is 19.46.
causal.assumptions_wrong_or_underweighted: Underweighted how fast a hot US inflation path would dominate a small NZD bounce through the dollar, and treated NZD spot as a substitute for the rates view once SOFR was the actual invalidation gauge.
causal.causal_divergence: The bounce was a fade of a dollar squeeze. The squeeze resumed because the US front end repriced higher, so the long never left the entry and the later spot is softer.
causal.future_implication: Leave NZDUSD alone while March 2027 SOFR holds above 4.435. The held SOFR, AONIA, and CORRA payers are the expression of resilient nominal growth.
causal.observed_reality: The long was exited at 0.56. NZDUSD is now 0.5584, March 2027 SOFR is 4.53, and the dollar is breaking up against the euro, the Australian dollar, and the Canadian dollar while equities and VIX have not signaled a growth break.
causal.original_belief: A long NZDUSD from 0.56 would extend if global risk appetite stayed intact and the bounce held.
causal.same_information_counterfactual: With the same growth view and the same SOFR invalidation level, the position to keep was the US front-end short, not a new NZDUSD long.

facts.invalidation: NZDUSD fully retraces the 1.26 percent bounce, or March 2027 SOFR trades up through the September 2027 mark at 4.435 and the dollar squeeze overwhelms the re-rating.

items.no_new_lesson: This was bounded variance around a rule that already existed. The invalidation was a full retrace of the bounce or March 2027 SOFR through 4.435 in a dollar squeeze, and the scratch followed that rule before the cross could become a loss. The prior process remains sound: do not reopen NZDUSD while that dollar-squeeze condition is live, and keep the pro-growth expression in the rates book.
items.thesis_assessment: The NZDUSD long was a bounce off 0.56 that never extended. It was scratched at the entry, and by this cutoff March 2027 SOFR is 4.53, through 4.435, with NZDUSD at 0.5584.
items.what_failed: The bounce failed to extend, but the pre-committed exit contained it at the entry price. The miss was using NZD spot to express a view whose real trigger was the US front end.

causal.assumptions_right: Risk appetite stayed expansionary, with the S&P at 7562 and the VIX at 18.7, and the US hike complex is still confirmed by Friday's higher yields.
causal.assumptions_wrong_or_underweighted: Oil was treated as persistent enough to carry a Canadian pay. The drop out of the scare zone, and Canada's oil beta, were underweighted.
causal.causal_divergence: The position lost money because the commodity catalyst faded inside a hike path that was already largely priced, while global growth did not collapse.
causal.future_implication: Do not reopen the Canada pay and do not add the Australia or US pays just because the US growth tape is intact.
causal.observed_reality: The short was closed after oil had fallen to WTI 88.56 and Brent 95.84, while March Canada bills were still near 3.03 against cash near 2.30.
causal.original_belief: A resilient growth tape plus oil in a scare zone would keep the Bank of Canada repricing the March 2027 bill higher from cash near 2.30 percent.
causal.same_information_counterfactual: With oil already off the scare and Canada inflation not yet in the evidence, the same information said to leave the Canada pay closed and keep the US SOFR pay.

facts.invalidation: CORRA_2027-03 back to the 2.775 Dec-26 3m mid or confirmed on-hold with core near 2% and fading oil.

items.future_rule: Do not reopen or add a Canada pay while Brent is around 96 and WTI around 89. Keep the US SOFR pay that Friday's fixings still support, and do not treat a stronger score as permission to add.
items.lesson: Do not treat a commodity-central-bank pay as the growth expression once oil has left the scare zone and the hike is already in the US strip.
items.thesis_assessment: The Canada pay was a pro-growth hike expression that needed a sustained oil impulse, and that impulse did not hold.
items.what_failed: Oil cooled from the old scare to WTI 88.56 and Brent 95.84, and the short March 2027 Canada bill was closed while the curve still priced hikes.

causal.assumptions_right: The front end could reprice higher without a growth collapse. Equities are still high and the U.S. minutes have leaned toward more hikes, which is consistent with a higher path.
causal.assumptions_wrong_or_underweighted: The oil spike and the low-vol reading were overweighted. A plain hawkish shift in the reaction function was underweighted, and that is what lifted implied rates.
causal.causal_divergence: The short moved because expected policy rates rose. The oil-and-vol scenario used as the exit never arrived, so the written invalidation described a different regime from the live driver.
causal.future_implication: A later Australian front-end pay should be exited off the cash-rate path and the growth data. It should not be re-shorted just because 4.905 is above the old entry.
causal.observed_reality: Implied rose to 4.92 at the exit and is still 4.905. Brent is 91.95 and equity vol is 25.46, so the contract stayed higher without the spike-and-complacency regime that was written down.
causal.original_belief: March 2027 Australian overnight rates at 4.76 looked too low if growth held up. An oil spike and depressed equity volatility were treated as the conditions that would make the pay unsafe.
causal.same_information_counterfactual: Brent at 91.95 and equity vol at 25.46 did not meet the stated invalidation, and implied was still well above 4.76. The same information supported keeping the pay under a rate-path rule.

facts.invalidation: Cover the new AONIA pay if March implied moves back to cash 4.60 without a higher cash rate, or if an energy and risk break from Brent 109.86, the S&P near 7659, and VIX 16.46 would justify Australian cuts rather than catch-up hikes. The Canada short is separately wrong if CORRA March keeps falling toward cash 2.27.

items.future_rule: Cover a short March Australian overnight rate only if implied falls back through the entry because the hike lean fades, or if Australian growth breaks while front-end implied is already elevated.
items.lesson: A front-end pay is invalidated by the policy path and by growth, not by a commodity extreme that is not the binding constraint.
items.thesis_assessment: The belief that the Australian front end was too low versus a still-restrictive path was right. The regime filter attached to that belief described a different world from the one that repriced the contract.
items.what_failed: The written invalidation was an oil spike and a low equity-vol reading. Brent is 91.95 and equity vol is 25.46, so the risk that was supposed to end the short never printed.
items.what_worked: The March 2027 Australian overnight-rate short was the right direction. Implied rose from 4.76 at entry to 4.92 at the exit and is still 4.905.

causal.assumptions_right: Front-end funding could reprice higher without an equity break. The equity market still fits a growth tape that can live with a higher policy path.
causal.assumptions_wrong_or_underweighted: The first two basis points were treated as enough of the move. How far a still-active hike lean could carry March, from 4.54 on to 4.575, was underweighted.
causal.causal_divergence: The direction matched the reaction function. The error was the exit clock: the cover happened while the same hike lean was still pushing the implied rate higher.
causal.future_implication: A future short in March secured funding needs a pre-committed path rule. It should not be chased at 4.575 merely to replace the early exit.
causal.observed_reality: Implied rose from 4.52 to 4.54 at the exit and now stands at 4.575. The minutes have leaned toward more hikes, and equities are still elevated.
causal.original_belief: March 2027 secured funding at 4.52 looked too low for an expansion that would keep policy restrictive. The pay was meant to work if growth stayed intact.
causal.same_information_counterfactual: At the exit the implied rate was only 4.54 against a 4.52 entry and restriction was not being walked back. The same information supported holding the pay.

facts.invalidation: The pay-STIR book is wrong if SOFR March 2027 moves down from 4.52 because the strip fully validates skip-October and removes December, or if WTI 103.66 and Brent 109.55 reverse while VIX 18.44 reprices as a growth scare. Cover CORRA March 2027 only if cash CORRA 2.26 versus the 3.01 March contract implies the Canadian hike path is abandoned despite oil. Do not use a 105 WTI headline as a trigger; stops and targets are null.

items.future_rule: Do not cover a short March 2027 secured-funding contract after a roughly two-basis-point rise while communication still leans toward more hikes. Keep it until implied reverses through the entry or the hike lean is walked back.
items.lesson: A small rise in implied secured funding is not a reason to cover a pay while the central bank is still leaning toward more hikes and equities have not broken.
items.thesis_assessment: Paying March because restriction would stick was a sound expression, and the later path confirmed it. The thesis held. The holding period did not.
items.what_failed: The cover at 4.54 treated a two-basis-point rise as a completed move. The later lift to 4.575 showed the exit came before the hawkish communication was in the front end.
items.what_worked: The March 2027 secured-funding short was the right pro-growth rates expression. Implied rose from 4.52 to 4.54 at the exit and has since reached 4.575.

causal.assumptions_right: The invalidation was correctly tied to a further downside break in AUDUSD occurring together with a higher SOFR March 2027 settle, and that combination ended the trade.
causal.assumptions_wrong_or_underweighted: The view underweighted the chance that a higher SOFR March settle would dominate AUDUSD, so pro-growth resilience did not show up in that pair.
causal.causal_divergence: AUDUSD fell from 0.68 to 0.67 instead of rising, and the decline lined up with SOFR March 2027 settling up.
causal.future_implication: When SOFR March is settling higher, a pro-growth view belongs in a currency whose defensive cheapness is extreme or in the rate itself, rather than in a cyclical dollar pair that is breaking down.
causal.observed_reality: AUDUSD was closed on 19 November at 0.67 after a further downside break, and SOFR March 2027 settled up on the same episode.
causal.original_belief: A long in AUDUSD from 0.68 would gain if underappreciated global growth pulled that pro-cyclical currency higher.
causal.same_information_counterfactual: With the same growth view and the same higher SOFR March settle, expressing the view somewhere other than AUDUSD would have avoided the move from 0.68 to 0.67.

items.expression_assessment: AUDUSD was a weak pro-growth sleeve because the pair fell from 0.68 to 0.67 and the stated invalidation, a further downside break while SOFR March 2027 settled up, fired together.

facts.invalidation: AUDUSD extends its 20-day downside break while SOFR March 2027 settles up through the June-September strip, so the yield backup becomes a parallel tightening shock.

items.no_new_lesson: The loss from 0.68 to 0.67 is bounded variance around a stop that fired on its stated condition, a further AUDUSD downside break with SOFR March 2027 settling up, so the process remains sound.

causal.assumptions_right: The hike-sensitive part of the SOFR strip could still move higher from 4.71, and the three-basis-point rise confirmed that belief.
causal.assumptions_wrong_or_underweighted: Follow-through beyond 4.74 was unknown, and a haven bid that pulls yields down was an underweighted way for a correct hike view to stall.
causal.causal_divergence: The position moved in the expected direction by three basis points and the close banked that move rather than leaving it exposed to a later haven-driven decline in yields.
causal.future_implication: A completed rise in September 2027 SOFR should be realized, and the next pro-growth expression should move to the market that now shows the excessive defensive price.
causal.observed_reality: The long was closed on 19 November after the mark had risen from 4.71 to 4.74.
causal.original_belief: A long in September 2027 SOFR from 4.71 would gain if a Fed still willing to discuss further hikes pulled that implied rate higher.
causal.same_information_counterfactual: With the rise from 4.71 to 4.74 already in hand, holding for a larger move would have turned a confirmed thesis into an open bet on follow-through that the close did not require.

items.expression_assessment: SOFR September 2027 was a sound rates sleeve for a growth-and-hikes view, because the long rose from 4.71 to 4.74 and was closed with that gain realized.

facts.invalidation: The September receive is invalidated if that contract holds 4.710 and the strip pushes further, or if oil moves back toward the prior scare zone. The Australian-dollar hold is invalidated if spot fails to stabilize while March SOFR at 4.545 and September at 4.710 hold the repricing.

items.no_new_lesson: A three-basis-point gain that was closed on a completed mark is bounded variance around a sound process, and the process remains sound without a new rule to stay long that contract.

causal.assumptions_right: The euro rule was right to define a close below 1.0992, with gold still elevated and VIX still in the mid-20s, as a defensive dollar bid. That same euro rule correctly forced the exit once the euro finished below 1.0992 and those defensive conditions were still present.
causal.assumptions_wrong_or_underweighted: The euro entry underweighted how quickly the rule's defensive-dollar test could print, treating euro weakness as growth the market had not yet priced. The euro did not rebound as underpriced growth, and the rule's close below 1.0992 arrived with gold and VIX still in the defensive zone.
causal.causal_divergence: The euro was expected to recover if the weakness was underpriced growth, but the euro closed below the rule's 1.0992 line instead. The divergence is the euro rule firing on a defensive dollar bid, with gold still elevated and VIX still in the mid-20s, rather than a growth bid showing up in the euro.
causal.future_implication: The euro stays governed by the same rule, so another close below 1.0992 with gold elevated and VIX in the mid-20s is still a defensive dollar bid. The implication is to leave the closed euro alone under that rule, and not to rewrite the rule from an exit that followed it.
causal.observed_reality: The euro is at 1.0975, through the rule's 1.0992 close, and gold at 3535.80 with VIX at 26.36 still meets the elevated-gold and mid-20s VIX part of the euro rule. The euro long was closed on 25 November because the rule had already been satisfied.
causal.original_belief: The euro long, opened on 20 November, assumed euro cheapness was underpriced growth, and the rule was the check on that belief. That euro rule required a close below 1.0992 with gold still elevated and VIX still in the mid-20s before a defensive dollar bid replaced the growth belief.
causal.same_information_counterfactual: On the same information, the euro long still had to come off once the rule printed a close below 1.0992 with gold elevated and VIX in the mid-20s. Holding the euro through that rule would have kept a ticket the rule had already classified as a defensive dollar bid.

items.expression_assessment: The euro long was the expression of the growth belief, and the rule was bound to the euro price rather than to a different instrument. The euro expression was adequate because the break of 1.0992 let the rule take the position off without a second decision.

facts.invalidation: A closing break of EURUSD below 1.0992, with gold still elevated and VIX still above the mid-20s, would show the defensive dollar bid is a trend rather than a discount of growth.

items.no_new_lesson: The euro was closed because the precommitted rule was met, a close below 1.0992 with gold still elevated and VIX still in the mid-20s, and that outcome is ordinary variance around a test defined in advance. The original process remains sound, so this euro exit under that rule does not become a new standing instruction.
items.thesis_assessment: The euro thesis claimed cheapness was underpriced growth, and the rule said a close below 1.0992 with gold elevated and VIX in the mid-20s would show a defensive dollar bid instead. That euro thesis was wrong, and the 25 November close obeyed the rule.
items.what_failed: The euro growth thesis failed when the euro closed below 1.0992 while the rule's gold and VIX conditions were still in place. The failure sits in the euro belief, while the rule itself did the exit it was written to do.
